name: Hebrew Decoding Ladder
principle: Decoding is prior to reading: recognize the letter and its sound, the vowel and its sound, then blend them. Genre-less phonics, kept separate from the capability-first foundation graph, which it gates into once a learner can decode.
promise: You can sound out a vocalized Hebrew word you have never seen.

masteryScale.emerging: Can do it with support and time.
masteryScale.secure: Can do it reliably and unaided.
masteryScale.transfer: Can do it in a word or setting not practiced.

durabilityTiers.foundation: Never lapses without the whole skill collapsing; drilled to automaticity.
durabilityTiers.core: Reviewed on a spaced schedule until automatic.

bands.title: Letters
bands.intent: Recognize and name the 22 letters, the 5 final forms, the sound-changing dots, and the silent carriers; tell the look-alikes apart.

bands.title: Vowels
bands.intent: Read the nikud vowel signs by sound family, plus shva, the reduced vowels, and the kamatz that says 'o'.

bands.title: Blending
bands.intent: Combine consonant and vowel into syllables and read a multi-syllable vocalized word.

bands.title: Sight & function words
bands.intent: Read the one-letter prefixes and the highest-frequency function words by sight, including the divine-name conventions and the common Aramaic particles of the Gemara.

bands.title: Vocalized fluency
bands.intent: Read short vocalized phrases and full verses from the siddur and Chumash at a comfortable pace, and self-correct a misread.

bands.title: Into the unvocalized
bands.intent: Read Hebrew without nikud — recognize known words, supply likely vowels from context, and begin a real Mishnah or Gemara line. This is the graduation into the foundation reading skills.

graduationContract.note: Graduation: read a short UNVOCALIZED Hebrew/Aramaic line — the way the Mishnah and Gemara actually print — well enough to begin studying it. That is the threshold into the foundation reading graph (fnd-signal-known-words and the Layer 1 orientation skills). Demonstrated across blending a vocalized word, reading a full vocalized verse, and reading an unvocalized line.

skills.title: Name the first letters (alef–zayin)
skills.statement: You can recognize and name alef, bet, gimel, dalet, hey, vav, and zayin.
skills.teachingMove: Meet the letters in a small group; say each name aloud while tracing its shape, and pair it with the sound it makes.
checks: Name five of the first seven letters shown out of order.
skills.transfer: Spot these letters inside a word you were not taught.
skills.repair: Return to the one or two letters you missed and trace each again before adding more.

skills.title: Name the middle letters (chet–nun)
skills.statement: You can recognize and name chet, tet, yod, kaf, lamed, mem, and nun.
skills.teachingMove: Add the next group the same way, and notice which ones resemble letters you already know.
checks: Name five of these seven letters shown out of order.
skills.transfer: Find one of these letters in a real word.
skills.repair: Drill the missed letter against the earlier letter it resembles.

skills.title: Name the last letters (samech–tav)
skills.statement: You can recognize and name samech, ayin, pei, tzadi, kuf, resh, shin, and tav.
skills.teachingMove: Complete the alef-bet, then shuffle all 22 and name them at random.
checks: Name six letters drawn from the whole alef-bet.
skills.transfer: Read the letters of an unfamiliar short word aloud, ignoring vowels.
skills.repair: Rebuild the full alef-bet in order, then test the letters you dropped.

skills.title: Recognize the five final forms
skills.statement: You can recognize the five sofit forms — ך ם ן ף ץ — and know they appear only at the end of a word.
skills.teachingMove: Match each final form to its regular twin (mem→ם, nun→ן, and so on) and note it only ever closes a word.
checks: Match three final forms to their regular letters.
skills.transfer: Point out a final letter at the end of a word in a real line.
skills.repair: Write the twin and the final form side by side and say they are the same letter.

skills.title: Tell apart the look-alike letters
skills.statement: You can distinguish the commonly confused letters: bet/kaf, dalet/resh, hey/chet/tav, vav/zayin/final-nun, gimel/nun, samech/final-mem.
skills.teachingMove: For each pair name the one visible difference — a heel, a corner, a gap, a crown — and check it every time.
checks: Given a look-alike pair, say which is which and name the difference.
skills.transfer: Correctly read a look-alike letter inside an unfamiliar word.
skills.repair: Isolate the one pair you confuse and drill only that pair.

skills.title: Hear the dagesh: bet/vet, kaf/chaf, pei/fei
skills.statement: You can tell that a dot inside bet, kaf, or pei hardens the sound (b, k, p) and that its absence softens it (v, kh, f).
skills.teachingMove: Show each letter with and without the dot and say both sounds; only these three letters change audibly in Modern Hebrew.
checks: Given bet/vet (or kaf/chaf, pei/fei), say which has the dot and which sound it makes.
skills.transfer: Read the right sound for one of these letters in an unfamiliar word.
skills.repair: Say the pair aloud — 'b, v' — while pointing to the dot and its absence.

skills.title: Read the shin dot and the sin dot
skills.statement: You can tell shin (שׁ, 'sh') from sin (שׂ, 's') by which side the dot sits on.
skills.teachingMove: Dot on the upper right = shin ('sh'); dot on the upper left = sin ('s'). Say each while pointing to its dot.
checks: Given a pointed shin/sin, say its sound.
skills.transfer: Read the correct sound in an unfamiliar word beginning with the letter.
skills.repair: Anchor it: shin/right/'sh' — three things on the same side.

skills.title: Read alef and ayin as silent carriers
skills.statement: You can treat alef (א) and ayin (ע) as silent letters that carry a vowel rather than adding a consonant sound.
skills.teachingMove: Show alef/ayin with a vowel and pronounce only the vowel; the letter is a seat, not a sound.
checks: Read alef and ayin with a vowel, producing only the vowel sound.
skills.transfer: Read a word that opens with a vowel-bearing alef or ayin.
skills.repair: Cover the letter and read just the vowel, then restore the letter unchanged.

skills.title: Read the 'a' vowels (kamatz, patach)
skills.statement: You can read kamatz (ָ) and patach (ַ) as the vowel 'a'.
skills.teachingMove: Place the mark under a known consonant and say the consonant plus 'a'; two different signs, one 'a' sound.
checks: Read three known consonants each carrying an 'a' vowel.
skills.transfer: Read an 'a' vowel on a letter you did not drill it with.
skills.repair: Go back to a single consonant + 'a' and rebuild.

skills.title: Read the 'e' vowels (tzere, segol)
skills.statement: You can read tzere (ֵ, two dots) and segol (ֶ, three dots) as the vowel 'e'.
skills.teachingMove: Count the dots to name the sign, then say the consonant plus 'e'; both signs say 'e'.
checks: Read a consonant with tzere and one with segol.
skills.transfer: Read an 'e' vowel in an unfamiliar syllable.
skills.repair: Separate tzere (2 dots) from segol (3 dots) by counting before sounding.

skills.title: Read the 'i' vowel (chirik)
skills.statement: You can read chirik (ִ, a single dot beneath a letter) as the vowel 'i'.
skills.teachingMove: One dot directly under the letter says 'i' (as in 'machine'); contrast it with the dot-count of segol.
checks: Read two consonants carrying chirik.
skills.transfer: Read a chirik in an unfamiliar word.
skills.repair: Compare a lone dot (chirik, 'i') with two dots (tzere, 'e').

skills.title: Read the 'o' vowel (cholam)
skills.statement: You can read cholam as the vowel 'o', whether as a dot above-left (ֹ) or written full with vav (וֹ).
skills.teachingMove: A dot at the upper left of a letter, or a vav topped by a dot, both say 'o'.
checks: Read a defective cholam and a full cholam (with vav).
skills.transfer: Read an 'o' vowel in an unfamiliar word.
skills.repair: Note the dot's high-left position so you do not read it as a letter's own dot.

skills.title: Read the 'u' vowels (kubutz, shuruk)
skills.statement: You can read kubutz (ֻ, three diagonal dots beneath) and shuruk (וּ, a vav with a dot in its side) as the vowel 'u'.
skills.teachingMove: Both say 'u'; shuruk rides on a vav with a centered dot, kubutz sits as three dots under the letter.
checks: Read a consonant with kubutz and a vav-shuruk.
skills.transfer: Read a 'u' vowel in an unfamiliar word.
skills.repair: Distinguish shuruk's centered dot from cholam's high-left dot on the vav.

skills.title: Read the shva (na vs nach)
skills.statement: You can read shva (ְ) and tell a sounded shva (na, a very short 'e') from a silent one (nach).
skills.teachingMove: Two vertical dots. It is sounded at the start of a word or as the second of two shvas, and silent when it closes a syllable — learn the common cases first.
checks: Given a word-initial shva and a syllable-closing shva, say which is sounded.
skills.transfer: Judge a shva correctly in an unfamiliar word.
skills.repair: Fall back to the rule of thumb: opening shva sounds, closing shva is silent.

skills.title: Read the reduced (chataf) vowels
skills.statement: You can read the chataf vowels (ֲ ֱ ֳ) under the guttural letters as a very short a, e, or o.
skills.teachingMove: A shva paired with a small vowel makes a hurried version of that vowel, found under alef, hey, chet, and ayin.
checks: Read a guttural carrying a chataf-patach and name the short vowel.
skills.transfer: Read a chataf vowel in an unfamiliar word.
skills.repair: Read the paired vowel plainly first, then shorten it.

skills.title: Spot the kamatz that says 'o'
skills.statement: You can recognize a kamatz katan — a kamatz (ָ) pronounced 'o' rather than 'a' — in its common patterns.
skills.teachingMove: In an unstressed closed syllable a kamatz says 'o' (kol, chol-mah); learn the frequent words rather than every rule at first.
checks: Read a common kamatz-katan word ('o') and a plain kamatz word ('a').
skills.transfer: Judge a kamatz correctly in an unfamiliar closed syllable.
skills.repair: Memorize a short list of everyday kamatz-katan words as anchors.

skills.title: Blend an open syllable (consonant + vowel)
skills.statement: You can blend a consonant and a vowel into an open syllable, like בָּ → 'ba'.
skills.teachingMove: Say the consonant sound and the vowel sound, then slide them together with no gap.
checks: Blend three consonant-plus-vowel pairs aloud.
skills.transfer: Blend an open syllable you did not drill.
skills.repair: Slow down: sound the consonant, sound the vowel, then join them.

skills.title: Blend a closed syllable (consonant + vowel + consonant)
skills.statement: You can blend a closed syllable, like בַּת → 'bat', where a consonant follows the vowel.
skills.teachingMove: Build the open syllable, then add the closing consonant's sound onto its end.
checks: Read three closed syllables aloud.
skills.transfer: Read a closed syllable in an unfamiliar word.
skills.repair: Split it: read the open syllable, then attach the final consonant.

skills.title: Handle a doubling dagesh
skills.statement: You can recognize a dagesh chazak that doubles a letter and read across it without stumbling.
skills.teachingMove: A dot in a letter that is not bet/kaf/pei, or after a vowel, doubles the letter — it closes one syllable and opens the next.
checks: Read a word with a doubling dagesh, splitting the syllable at the dot.
skills.transfer: Read a doubled letter in an unfamiliar word.
skills.repair: Treat the dotted letter as written twice: once closing, once opening.

skills.title: Blend with a shva inside a word
skills.statement: You can decide whether a shva mid-word is sounded or silent and blend the word accordingly.
skills.teachingMove: Apply the shva rule inside a real word: a sounded shva starts a new short syllable; a silent one just closes the last one.
checks: Read a two-syllable word whose split depends on a shva.
skills.transfer: Blend an unfamiliar word containing a shva.
skills.repair: Read both ways aloud and keep the one that matches a real word.

skills.title: Read a pronounced final hey (mapik)
skills.statement: You can recognize a mapik he (הּ) and pronounce the final hey instead of leaving it silent.
skills.teachingMove: A dot inside a word-final hey means it is a real consonant 'h' to be sounded, not a silent vowel-letter.
checks: Read a word ending in mapik he, sounding the final 'h'.
skills.transfer: Read a mapik he in an unfamiliar word.
skills.repair: Contrast a plain final hey (silent) with a dotted one (sounded).

skills.title: Read a multi-syllable vocalized word
skills.statement: You can read a two- or three-syllable vocalized word, moving right to left one syllable at a time.
skills.teachingMove: Break the word into syllables at each vowel, read each syllable, then say them in sequence at pace.
checks: Read a three-syllable vocalized word aloud.
skills.transfer: Read an unfamiliar multi-syllable vocalized word.
skills.repair: Mark the syllable breaks with a finger before sounding the word.

skills.title: Read a furtive patach
skills.statement: You can read a furtive patach — an 'a' slipped in before a final guttural, as in רוּחַ → 'ruach'.
skills.teachingMove: A patach under a final chet, ayin, or hey is pronounced BEFORE that letter, not after it.
checks: Read a word ending in a furtive patach ('...ach', '...ea').
skills.transfer: Read a furtive patach in an unfamiliar word.
skills.repair: Say the vowel before the guttural and let the guttural close the word.

skills.title: Read the one-letter prefixes
skills.statement: You can read the one-letter prefixes attached to the front of a word: ה (the), ו (and), and בְּ / כְּ / לְ / מִ / שֶׁ (in / like / to / from / that).
skills.teachingMove: Peel the first letter off a familiar word and name the little word it adds: the, and, in, to, from, like, that.
checks: Given a prefixed word, say the prefix's meaning and the base word.
skills.transfer: Strip the prefix from an unfamiliar word and read the base.
skills.repair: Cover the first letter, read the base word, then add the prefix back.

skills.title: Read high-frequency words by sight
skills.statement: You can recognize the most common function words at a glance — אֶת, כִּי, אֲשֶׁר, אֶל, עַל, מִן, כָּל, לֹא, אִם — instead of sounding them out letter by letter.
skills.teachingMove: Drill the twenty most frequent little words until each is recognized whole, as a shape, not decoded.
checks: Read five function words at a glance and give each meaning.
skills.transfer: Spot a known function word inside an unfamiliar sentence.
skills.repair: Decode the word slowly once, then add it to a sight-word list to over-learn.

skills.title: Recognize the object marker את
skills.statement: You can recognize אֶת and read past it, knowing it marks a definite direct object and has no English word of its own.
skills.teachingMove: When you meet אֶת, treat the noun after it as what the verb acts on, and do not hunt for an English translation of אֶת itself.
checks: Point to what אֶת marks in a short clause.
skills.transfer: Read an unfamiliar clause containing אֶת without stumbling.
skills.repair: Read the clause aloud skipping אֶת and confirm it still makes sense.

skills.title: Read the divine-name conventions
skills.statement: You can recognize the four-letter Name (יהוה) and read it as 'Adonai' (or 'Hashem'), and recognize אֱלֹהִים, rather than pronouncing the Name as it is spelled.
skills.teachingMove: Learn that the four-letter Name is not pronounced as written; it is read 'Adonai' in prayer and study, and 'Hashem' in casual reference.
checks: On meeting the Name, say how it is read aloud and why.
skills.transfer: Handle the Name correctly in an unfamiliar verse.
skills.repair: Ask whether the setting is prayer or study ('Adonai') or casual reference ('Hashem').

skills.title: Recognize the common Aramaic particles
skills.statement: You can recognize the high-frequency Aramaic particles of the Gemara — the prefix דְּ ('that / of / which') and words like מַאי ('what') — as the connective glue of a sugya.
skills.teachingMove: Learn a short set of Aramaic function words as a family; the prefix דְּ especially links clause after clause.
checks: Given an Aramaic phrase, point out the דְּ and say roughly what it links.
skills.transfer: Spot דְּ and one other particle in an unfamiliar Gemara line.
skills.repair: Read the דְּ as 'that / of' and check whether the clause connects.

skills.title: Read a vocalized phrase at pace
skills.statement: You can read a short, fully vocalized phrase from the siddur or Chumash aloud at a comfortable pace, without stalling on every letter.
skills.teachingMove: Read in syllable-groups, not letter by letter; let words you know come as wholes.
checks: Read a two-to-four-word vocalized phrase aloud in one pass.
skills.transfer: Read an unfamiliar short vocalized phrase at pace.
skills.repair: Slow to syllables for the one hard word, then re-read the whole phrase.

skills.title: Catch and fix a misread
skills.statement: You can notice when a word you read is not a real word, and re-check its letters and vowels to fix it.
skills.teachingMove: Trust your ear: if what you produced is not a word, go back and find the vowel or letter you misread.
checks: Given a deliberately misread word, find and fix the error.
skills.transfer: Self-correct inside an unfamiliar phrase.
skills.repair: Isolate the syllable that sounded wrong and re-decode just that one.

skills.title: Read a full vocalized verse
skills.statement: You can read a full vocalized verse — such as the first line of the Shema — from beginning to end.
skills.teachingMove: Chain the phrases: read each phrase you can, then join them into the whole verse.
checks: Read one full vocalized verse aloud.
skills.transfer: Read an unfamiliar full vocalized verse.
skills.repair: Break the verse at its phrase boundaries and read one phrase at a time.

skills.title: Recognize a known word without vowels
skills.statement: You can recognize a word you already know when it appears without its vowels, supplying the vowels yourself.
skills.teachingMove: Read the consonant skeleton of a familiar word and let the vowels you already know fill themselves in.
checks: Match three unvocalized words to their vocalized forms.
skills.transfer: Recognize a known word unvocalized in a new setting.
skills.repair: Write the word with its vowels, then remove them and read it again.

skills.title: Supply the likely vowels from context
skills.statement: You can supply the most likely vowels for an unvocalized word from its shape and its context, choosing among the readings its consonants allow.
skills.teachingMove: When an unvocalized word has more than one reading, let the sentence decide which fits — a noun, a verb, a name.
checks: Given an ambiguous unvocalized word in a sentence, choose the reading that fits.
skills.transfer: Resolve an unfamiliar unvocalized word from context.
skills.repair: List the two readings the consonants allow and test each against the sentence.

skills.title: Read a short unvocalized line
skills.statement: You can read a short unvocalized Hebrew or Aramaic line — the way the Mishnah and Gemara actually print — well enough to begin studying it. This is the threshold into the foundation reading skills.
skills.teachingMove: Read the consonants, recognize the words you know, supply the vowels from context, and read the line as a whole.
checks: Read a short unvocalized Mishnah or Gemara phrase and say what it says.
skills.transfer: Begin an unfamiliar short unvocalized line.
skills.repair: Vocalize the one word you cannot place, then re-read the line.
